caption:
Everyone's heard of Otter. Almost nobody's talking about the notetaker that a huge share of real users say quietly beat it.

Fathom joins your Zoom, Google Meet, or Microsoft Teams call, records it, and writes an AI summary the second the call ends. That part alone would be useful. What makes it strange in a good way: every line of that summary is timestamped, so you can click a single sentence and it jumps straight back into the recording and replays that exact moment. No more "wait, what did they actually say?" three days later.

It also holds a conversation about your own meeting history. Ask it "what did we agree on pricing last month?" and it answers from the real transcript, not a guess.

It's not invisible — it shows up in the call as "Fathom Notetaker" so everyone knows it's there, and like any transcription tool it can slip a little in messy audio. But that transparency is part of why it's built up over 6,000 reviews on G2 with a full 5.0 average, plus a string of independent head-to-head comparisons against Otter and Fireflies.

Think beyond work calls too: job interviews, therapy or coaching sessions, a family Zoom with a lawyer or doctor — any conversation where you'd rather be present than scribbling. And the free tier is genuinely generous, not a countdown clock, which is a big part of why people actually stick with it.
